plate.narration: A frogfolk ferrywoman pushes into the Whispering Marsh. Tiny bells hang from her ribbons. Beyond them, new wisps bob over the water, crowding close as if they have something to say. Where will the channel lead?

objectives.label: Saw through the mire mimic's act
Let a wisp show you what it remembers

goal.text: Ride through the Whispering Marsh and find a way out.

steps.label: Find a way through the fog
Choose a way out of the marsh

facet_barge.name: The Barge Stone
facet_barge.text: The one real prop in a mire mimic's act. It hums the same note as the Hollow Gate.

scene_poling_in.narration: Marda's rumor board said the frogfolk still ferry the ones they like. A ferrywoman called Gullet likes you. Tonight, ride with her through the Whispering Marsh and find a way out. New wisps crowd behind bell ribbons. "Too many," Gullet hums. "Ask the boggarts. They keep lost things."

scene_poling_in_say_it.narration: "Something's leaking," you say. The new wisps all turn toward you at once, like candles in a draft. Gullet carves a notch in her hat. "Not near the wisps," she says. "They remember things."

scene_unicorn_feels.narration: You lower your horn toward the ribbon, and the wisps go still. Each one is a tangled memory. Every one remembers the same night: red light falling from the sky, and for one moment, falling up.

scene_poling_in_pole_on.narration: "Gems are the most lost things this season," Gullet hums, steering for the boggarts' island. A frog salutes from a lily pad. She salutes back, just in case.

scene_ribbon_line.narration: Gullet's cousins are moving a bell ribbon across the channel. Their leader wears three hats. Help them and earn a dry crossing later, or duck under on your own. "Never through it," Gullet says.

check_ribbon_duck.prompt: Duck under the bell ribbon without making a jingle

onSuccess.narration: Everybody folds flat as a pancake. Not one jingle. On the far side of the ribbon, the new wisps bob up and down in a slow, polite round of applause, and the cousin in three hats tips all three.

onFailure.narration: Jingle. Jingle-jingle. Every bell on the line goes off at once. The new wisps all crowd to the ribbon to see who rang, and the ribbon crew, all together, say "Tsk." Gullet poles away very fast, pretending she has never met you.

scene_ribbon_line_help.narration: You hold the pole while the cousins retie their ribbon. "Good hands," croaks the cousin in three hats. "We will carry you across the weir later."

scene_ribbon_line_knots.narration: Your bigfoot crouches by the ribbon post. These are MossHome path-knots, tied by bigfoot to mean this way has moved. "Tall lady with cords," says a cousin. "Never stopped jogging."

scene_boggart_isle.narration: A boggart called Nana Rummage sorts lost things on her island: mittens, umbrellas, a teapot lid. A bag hums in her lap. "Trade, maybe," she tells a mitten. She wants an unusual sound.

check_trade.prompt: Poke through her piles and find the one lost thing Nana Rummage hasn't got

onSuccess.narration: It's the squeak your left boot makes. She wants the squeak. You give her a good long one, and she writes it down, delighted, and throws in a jar of mosslight she found last spring.

onFailure.narration: You offer a button, a pebble and half a sandwich. Wrong, wrong, and she eats the sandwich anyway. In the end she takes your best whistle-tune by humming it back at you until you give up, and calls it even.

scene_boggart_clue.narration: Nana opens her bag. A gem chip hums one low note. "Like the old Gate in the still water," she tells a teapot lid. "The Hollow Gate. Exactly the same." To an umbrella: "Not that I said."

scene_boggart_clue_thanks.narration: "Thank you," you tell the nearest umbrella. Nana is so pleased she nearly looks at you. She hands you a teapot lid, then takes it back. That is how boggarts say goodbye.

scene_boggart_clue_where.narration: Nana answers the mitten instead. "Barges are very convenient this season. Abandoned ones. Gem on the deck. Very, very convenient." The mitten says nothing. What did she mean?

scene_boggart_clue_lost.narration: Nana tells the teapot lid what she found: umbrellas, a brown hat, and three prospectors. "Barge spat them out. They're on a tussock north of here. Too loud for my collection."

scene_toll_reeds.narration: Knotted reeds block the channel. "Another toll," Gullet hums. A reed holds out its tip like a waiting hand. The knots tremble whenever somebody speaks.

check_toll_story.prompt: Tell the toll reeds a story good enough to pay your way

onSuccess.narration: You tell them about the time a goose chased you all the way around a market. The reeds lean in. At the bit with the cabbage they actually gasp. One by one they untie themselves to hear better, and by the end there is a clear channel and a lot of rustling that might be clapping.

onFailure.narration: You start well, then forget whether it was a goose or a duck, and then whether it happened to you at all. The reeds get bored. One slips the lace out of your boot as payment, and the channel opens with a sniff. That boot flaps for the rest of the day.

scene_toll_reeds_sock.narration: You pull off a sock and hold it up. The reeds go wild. They pass it reed to reed and hang it up like a flag. The knots fall open. Somebody has one cold foot all day.

scene_toll_reeds_salute.narration: You stand and give the harvest sprites' salute. Every growing thing knows it. The reeds untie at once and salute back so hard that one falls over.

scene_barge.narration: A barge sits in the reeds. ABANDONED, says its very helpful sign. One gem hums on deck. Prospector footprints lead toward it. None come back. "That is certainly a barge," Gullet hums.

scene_barge_convenient.narration: "Very convenient," you say loudly, like Nana. "An abandoned barge, with one gem on it." A barnacle blinks. The whole barge sighs, unfolds into an embarrassed mire mimic, and slides into the reeds.

check_name.prompt: Spot what's wrong with this barge, and say what it really is

onSuccess.narration: The barge has eyelashes. Barges do not have eyelashes. "You're a mire mimic," you say, and the whole barge sighs, unfolds into something long and muddy and embarrassed, and slides off into the reeds.

onFailure.narration: You lean in for a closer look, and the closer look opens its mouth.

check_stamp.prompt: Stamp the bank hard enough to shake a mimic off its patch

onSuccess.narration: You stamp, and stamp, and do a sort of stamping dance, and the barge starts to wobble. Then it stands up, on legs, and stalks off into the reeds, muttering about the state of modern audiences.

onFailure.narration: The bank shakes. So does the barge. Then the barge turns around and looks at you, and it is not pleased.

scene_kitsune_review.narration: Your kitsune circles the barge, nose in the air. "Barnacles on the wrong side. That rope is a tail. And nobody abandons a polished lantern." A wounded silence. The barge unfolds into a mire mimic and slinks off.

encounter_mimic.narration: The barge heaves up out of the mud on long gray legs. A wisp that has been leading prospectors this way drifts in to watch.

onVictory.narration: The mimic decides you are too much trouble and slithers off into the reeds.

onDefeat.narration: The mimic gulps the gem, spits you onto a mudbank, and sinks. The wisp drifts off, giggling. It's getting dark, and every channel looks the same.

check_find_way.prompt: Find your way back to the main channel in the dark

onSuccess.narration: You follow the sound of humming and a bobbing, notched hat. Gullet hauls you onto her raft and says nothing at all about the mud.

onFailure.narration: Every channel looks like every other channel, and the wisps keep swapping them around when you blink. By the time you give up and sit down on a tussock, the moon has set and the marsh has decided to keep you a little longer.

scene_act_closed.narration: The show is over. Where the barge sat, there is only mud, reeds, and one real gem. It hums like Nana's bag, steady as a heartbeat.

scene_act_closed_leave.narration: You leave the stone where it lies. Slowly the mud takes it, like a hand closing, until even the hum is gone. Gullet nods once, the way frogfolk nod at a thing done properly.

scene_act_closed_take.narration: You lift the Barge Stone out of the mud. It hums louder, as if pleased to be held. Every reed on the bank leans toward it, then away. Behind you, a long muddy shape sighs.

rest_reed_raft.narration: Gullet ties her raft to a lantern pole and fries duckweed fritters on a hot stone. They taste like crunchy pond. "Rest a while," she hums. But fog is rolling in, thick as porridge.

rest_reed_raft_hat.narration: Gullet turns her hat around. Every notch is a new wisp since the mountain went off. The brim is full. "When I run out of hat," she says, "I'll start on my other hat."

rest_reed_raft_on.narration: You curl up on the warm planks and wake with a frog on your chest, staring at you. It hops off. Gullet is untying the raft. The fog has arrived, and it brought friends.

scene_fog_bank.narration: Fog hides the channel fork and its stumps. "Which way, then?" Gullet hums. Follow a clear gap from the bow, steer by the bells behind you, or risk the wobbly high pole.

check_fog_lookout.prompt: Shin up the wobbly lantern pole and call out every stump in time

onSuccess.narration: "Stump left! Stump right! Heron!" You call them all, and Gullet threads the raft through like a needle through cloth. From the top of the pole you spot something else, too: a little island ahead, with people standing on it.

onFailure.narration: The pole wobbles, then leans, then lays you gently down in the reeds. From down there you can see under the fog perfectly, so you call out the stumps lying on your back. It works. It is just not very dignified. Then you hear grumbling ahead.

scene_fog_bank_listen.narration: Keep the ribbon bells behind you: that is the main channel. Gullet follows your pointing fingers around the stumps. Ahead, somebody grumbles. The fog still hides the landing.

scene_fog_bank_light.narration: You crack the mosslight jar. The fog clears for a raft's length, and you spot a broad landing beside an island. Somebody on the island is grumbling.

scene_tussock.narration: Three muddy prospectors balance on a sinking tussock. "Barge kept my good hat," says the tallest. Bring them aboard, and they may help you later. Or guide them out through the shallows.

check_tussock_haul.prompt: Haul three soggy prospectors onto a raft without tipping it over

onSuccess.narration: One heave, two heaves, and all three slide aboard like wet sacks of flour. The raft rides very low. Gullet drops them at a frogfolk landing where a path leads northeast toward the roads, and the tallest one gives you a squashed honeycake. "For the rescue. Sorry about the squash."

onFailure.narration: You grab the tallest one, he grabs you, and you both go in with a splash. The other two climb aboard over the top of you, saying sorry the whole way. Everybody ends up on the raft, equally wet, which feels fair. Gullet drops them at a landing with a path toward the northeast roads.

scene_tussock_nan.narration: "Nana Rummage has your hat," you say. The tallest gasps. Gullet sighs and poles them back to Nana's island for it. Then she drops them by a path to the northeast roads.

scene_tussock_shallows.narration: You point out the sandy shallows. The prospectors wade off and wave from safety. "Going home!" calls the tallest. "The rush can keep my hat."

scene_wisp_lead.narration: A wisp bobs ahead, then waits like a dog with a ball. Follow it patiently, hurry after it, or try saying please.

scene_wisp_lead_please.narration: "Please." The wisp goes pink, then gold. Nobody has asked it politely before. It glows in front of your face, ready to share a memory.

check_patience.prompt: Walk with the wisp, not after it, however slowly it goes

onSuccess.narration: It is slow. It is very, very slow. But it keeps looking back to check you're still there, and every time you are, it glows a little brighter.

onFailure.narration: Somebody sighs. The wisp hears it, takes offense, and takes a shortcut.

scene_wisp_trap.narration: The wisp leads you in a big loop, then into mud so sticky it keeps one boot each. The wisp looks smug. Across a stretch of still water stands something huge and gray.

scene_wisp_sight.narration: The wisp brightens, and you see its memory: a sky of falling red sparks, and one moment when every spark fell up. Then it leads you to the edge of the reeds. Across still water stands something enormous.

scene_old_steps.narration: Ancient stone steps cross the still water toward the huge gray shape. Their middles are worn smooth. A frog sits on the third step like it has a ticket.

check_steps_wade.prompt: Wade across the still water without slipping on the old steps

onSuccess.narration: Slow and steady, step by step. The water doesn't even ripple. It is like walking across a mirror, and in the mirror the sky is full of falling red sparks. You look up. It isn't. You look down. It is. You decide to stop looking down.

onFailure.narration: Somebody slips on the fourth step and sits down in the water with a great flat SPLOSH. It isn't deep. It is just extremely wet. The ripples run all the way to the gray shape and come back again, slowly, as if something over there gave them a gentle push home.

scene_old_steps_frog.narration: Asked politely, the frog hops onto your head. You cross the steps wearing it. Gullet approves. Frogfolk respect a good hat.

scene_hollow_gate.narration: The Hollow Gate stands in the still water, older than the marsh or the mountain's name. Its runes glow. Every reed around it is knotted. It does not open. It does not look as if it ever has.

scene_gate_hum.narration: The runes hum. It is the same note as Nana's bag and the barge's gem. Exactly the same. A door? A warning? The Gate does not explain. It keeps humming.

scene_gate_shard.narration: Half in the mud by the bottom step lies a curl of cold silver. When your boots come near, it hums once, the same note. Then it goes quiet.

scene_gate_shard_leave.narration: You leave it in the mud. The water closes over it without a ripple. The Gate hums on. You feel that something has been noted.

scene_gate_shard_pick_up.narration: You pick it up. It is cold and light. It hums once in your pocket, then settles like a bird. Behind you, one knotted reed unties itself. Nobody saw it. Everybody saw it.

choice_gate_record.narration: How will you remember the Gate? A braced rubbing keeps a checked shape. A shared note helps with the frogfolk's crossing song, but leaves no paper. Or count the reeds, or risk a quick rubbing.

check_gate_rubbing.prompt: Take a clean rubbing of a glowing rune without smudging it

onSuccess.narration: Paper flat, charcoal sideways, gentle as anything. The rune comes up black on white, curly and careful, like handwriting from somebody who meant every line. You roll it up. It doesn't hum. It is only paper. Somehow that makes it more important to keep.

onFailure.narration: The paper is damp, and the charcoal is damper, and what comes out is a very detailed picture of your own thumb. You keep it anyway. It is, after all, a thumb that has touched the Hollow Gate, and not many thumbs can say that.

check_gate_hum.prompt: Hum the Gate's note back to it, all on the same note

onSuccess.narration: You hum. For one long breath your note and the Gate's note are the same note, and every knotted reed around you shivers at once. Nothing opens. Nothing changes. But you could swear the hum is a little softer afterwards, like a kettle that has been taken off the boil.

onFailure.narration: You hum, and the notes wobble all over the place, and a frog on the old steps corrects you, loudly, with the right one. The Gate ignores the whole performance magnificently. You will remember that frog for the rest of your lives.

choice_gate_record_count.narration: You give up counting knotted reeds at three hundred and twelve. Far out, the knots are loose and lazy. Nearest the Gate, they are tight as fists. Whatever tangles the marsh, it tangles thickest here.

scene_nan_washtub.narration: Nana rows up in a washtub, paddling with a soup ladle. "Lost things drift here. More lately," she tells it. She fishes out a surprised fish, puts it back, and waits for your question.

scene_nan_washtub_north.narration: "The trees keep lost things too," Nana tells the ladle. "Not mittens. Humming things." She sniffs at their poor taste and rows backward into the fog.

scene_nan_washtub_road.narration: "Everybody on the roads is going the same way," Nana tells a spoon. "None of them knows they are lost." She rows backward into the fog.

choice_exit.narration: Choose your road. North, the frogfolk weir leads to the Enchanted Woods. Northeast, wheels and a sausage seller mean the rush road. Friends you made can help, but the road is yours to pick.

scene_reed_edge.narration: At the rush road, a sausage cart is stuck to its axles. "Free sausages for help!" pants the seller. A goose honks on behalf of the whole waiting line.

check_cart_push.prompt: Push a sausage cart out of marsh mud

onSuccess.narration: One, two, three, HEAVE. The cart pops out of the mud like a cork from a bottle, and the sausage seller hands out sausages hot off the griddle. The whole line cheers, and the goose is beside itself. Nobody has ever been welcomed onto a road this loudly.

onFailure.narration: You heave. The cart doesn't. Then three wagon drivers jump down to help, and the goose supervises, and between everybody it squelches free. The sausage seller gives everybody half a sausage each, which is the rush's idea of fair.

scene_reed_edge_reeds.narration: You carpet the mud with reeds. The cart rolls free. "Clever marsh folk!" shouts the seller, and hands over supper. The goose takes the credit.

scene_reed_edge_prospectors.narration: "Tussock people!" Your prospectors run from the line to push. The cart shoots free, and the seller brings back supper for everyone. The tallest prospector gets an extra sausage.

scene_west_branch.narration: The west branch runs wide and brown along the marsh's northern edge. Gullet's cousins have built a weir of poles and stepping stones. They wait on it in their best hats to pole you over.

scene_west_branch_crew.narration: The cousin in three hats spots you. "The good hands!" the cousins cry. They carry your raft across on their shoulders, singing, and set you down dry on the north bank. Gullet pretends not to be proud.

check_ford_song.prompt: Pole and stamp in time with the frogfolk's crossing song

onSuccess.narration: You sing badly but exactly in time, which is the part that counts.

onFailure.narration: Somebody sneezes on the wrong beat. The raft wobbles, and the river takes its chance.

check_ford_hop.prompt: Hop the weir stones across the west branch

onSuccess.narration: Stone, stone, pole, stone, and a big jump at the end. Nobody even gets a sock wet.

onFailure.narration: The fourth stone turns out to be a frog. It moves.

ending_forded_clean.narration: The frogfolk set you down dry on the north bank. Gullet waves her notched hat until the fog swallows her. Ahead, the Enchanted Woods stand very still, as if expecting you. You heard the note today. You won't forget it.

variants.text: Your checked rubbing shows the rune's shape, not its meaning.
Your rubbing was checked with Gullet's help.
You carry the shared beat in memory, without a paper rubbing.
Gullet helped hold your practice beat together.
Gullet helped you see through the pretend barge.

ending_swept_west.narration: The branch carries you west past floating logs (real ones, you check). You crawl out, soaked, at the edge of the Enchanted Woods, near MossHome, the bigfoot town. Late, dripping, and in. Wring out your socks and camp.

variants.text: Your checked rubbing shows the rune's shape, not its meaning.
Your rubbing was checked with Gullet's help.
You carry the shared beat in memory, without a paper rubbing.
Gullet helped hold your practice beat together.
Gullet helped you see through the pretend barge.

ending_walked_over.narration: You step off the mud onto a road full of wagons and fall in behind the sausage cart. Everybody here is going the same way, after the same stones. Behind you, faintly, the boggarts are laughing.

variants.text: Your checked rubbing shows the rune's shape, not its meaning.
Your rubbing was checked with Gullet's help.
You carry the shared beat in memory, without a paper rubbing.
Gullet helped hold your practice beat together.
Gullet helped you see through the pretend barge.

ending_marsh_kept_secrets.narration: In the dark every channel looks the same, and the wisps think it's a game. You never find the Gate. At dawn the current drops you, soggy and sorry, at the edge of the Enchanted Woods. The marsh kept its secrets.

scene_toll_reeds_coin.narration: You hold up a coin. A reed plucks it gently from your fingers, and the knots untie one by one. The coin is passed back to a nest, where it shines like a small moon.

interaction_wisp_crowd.narration: A crowd of new wisps follows your raft, bumping it like puppies. "Keep them busy till the island!" calls the cousin in three hats. "Bored wisps tie knots. Last week they tied my hats together."

interaction_reed_gap.narration: The reeds keep swinging shut, like doors in a draft. "Wait for it," Gullet hums. "Wait. Now!" Pole through when the gap is wide.

interaction.cue: Pole through when the gap in the reeds is wide open.

onSuccess.narration: Whoosh. The raft slides through with a hand's width to spare. Gullet pats her pole.

onFailure.narration: Slap! The reeds grab your hats. Gullet gets you through on the next swing, hair full of leaves.

onAssisted.narration: Gullet counts it out loud, and the raft slips right through.

interaction_lantern.narration: Gullet passes the lantern forward while you steady its hook. The fog stops at the edge of its glow like a shy cat. "Good hands," she says, and puts a jar of mosslight in your pack. "Fog gets thick past here."

interaction_stumps.narration: Somebody on the island ahead is grumbling. But first comes the biggest stump yet, rolling like a sleeping cow. "Fend it off!" hums Gullet. "One pushes. Everybody else keeps the raft still."

interaction.cue: Friends hold the raft steady while someone pushes the stump away.

onSuccess.narration: The stump turns slowly and drifts away, looking a little hurt. The raft barely rocks.

onFailure.narration: The stump shoves the raft. Everyone sits down at once, and a frog lands in someone's lap.

onAssisted.narration: Gullet braces the raft while you push. The stump drifts off, looking a little hurt.

interaction_runes.narration: As you step back, the Gate's runes glow one at a time. Tall rune, wavy rune, round rune. Watch the order, then trace it back.

interaction.cue: Watch the runes glow, then trace them back in the same order.

onSuccess.narration: Tall, wavy, round, wavy. The last rune glows a little longer. A frog on the steps nods.

onFailure.narration: You trace a different order. The Gate glows the right one once more, slowly, like showing someone how to tie a shoe.

scene_crab_shallows.narration: At the edge of the reeds, two young glassback crabs sit on an old stone step, clacking. They guard a heap of shiny lost things: spoons, buttons, a teapot lid. Your way goes right through them.

encounter_crabs.narration: The crabs rise up, clacking like castanets. Make them give up the steps.

scene_crabs_shooed.narration: The crabs scuttle into deep water and leave their heap. Gullet picks through it with her pole. "Spoons are Nana's. This whistle is nobody's." She tosses you a very loud tin whistle.

scene_crabs_rescue.narration: The crabs chase you off the steps, and you sit down in the shallows with a splash. Gullet hooks you out and hands out hot fritters. Soon the crabs wander off to guard a different puddle.

interaction_ribbon_duck.narration: The ribbon rises as the cousins shift their poles. Wait for a clear gap, then duck. The cousin in three hats folds almost flat. The hats do not.

interaction.cue: Duck when the marker is in the clear gap.

onSuccess.narration: Everybody folds flat as a pancake. Not one jingle. The new wisps bob in polite applause.

onFailure.narration: Jingle-jingle! Every bell goes off. The ribbon crew all say "Tsk." Gullet poles away fast.

onAssisted.narration: The cousin holds the ribbon high while you duck. You pass, but the crew owes you no favor.

interaction_fog_lookout.narration: Gullet points out a patch of clear water between drifting reed clumps. Follow it as the reeds slide past. Where it ends up, the raft can turn. A heron watches. It has no advice.

interaction.cue: Follow the clear-water glow. Choose its final position.

onSuccess.narration: You call the open channel. Gullet spots a broad landing beside a grumbling island.

onFailure.narration: That gap closes. Gullet feels her way to the muddy side of a grumbling island.

onAssisted.narration: Gullet points with her pole. Together you find a broad landing beside a grumbling island.

interaction_tussock_balance.narration: The prospectors climb aboard one at a time. Keep the raft level as each wet boot lands. The tallest says his hat was heavier than this.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side to keep the raft marker in the middle.

onSuccess.narration: They slide aboard like wet sacks of flour. Gullet drops them by a path to the northeast roads. The tallest gives you a squashed honeycake. "Sorry about the squash."

onFailure.narration: You and the tallest both go in with a splash. Everybody ends up equally wet. Gullet drops the prospectors by a path to the northeast roads.

onAssisted.narration: Gullet braces the raft while you balance. The prospectors leave at the northeast landing, and hand you a squashed honeycake.

scene_tussock_landing.narration: You bring the raft alongside the broad landing. The prospectors step aboard instead of leaping. Gullet drops them by the northeast road, and the tallest hands you a squashed honeycake.

interaction_gate_rubbing.narration: The paper wants to curl. The charcoal wants to roll. Hold the sheet flat while a friend rubs the rune, or use a flat stone. The frog watches your thumb closely.

interaction.cue: Hold the paper flat while the acting hero rubs the rune.

onSuccess.narration: The shape comes up clear, and you check it against the rune. This is what you saw. It is not an answer.

onFailure.narration: A very detailed thumbprint fills the paper. It is not a checked rune.

onAssisted.narration: Gullet pins the curling paper while you rub. The shape is checked with her help. What it means is still a mystery.

interaction_gate_hum.narration: Add a sound to the group's beat: hum, tap a knee, or breathe. The frog adds a loud croak, invited or not. This is practice for keeping together, not a singing test.

interaction_weir_song.narration: Gullet's cousins stamp their poles on the weir. Wait for the short gap between stamps, then move. One cousin's hats bounce on every beat.

interaction.cue: Pole across when the marker is inside the gold beat.

onSuccess.narration: Your poles land together. The raft clears the weir and reaches the north bank dry.

onFailure.narration: Your poles land off the beat. The raft wobbles, and the branch carries you west.

onAssisted.narration: Gullet calls each move while the cousins brace the weir. You reach the north bank dry.

interaction_weir_practiced.narration: Gullet's cousins stamp their poles on the weir. Your practiced beat gives you longer to move together. One cousin's hats bounce on every beat.

interaction.cue: Pole across when the marker is inside the gold beat.

onSuccess.narration: Your poles land together. The raft clears the weir and reaches the north bank dry.

onFailure.narration: Your poles land off the beat. The raft wobbles, and the branch carries you west.

onAssisted.narration: Gullet calls each move while the cousins brace the weir. You reach the north bank dry.

interaction_barge_audience.narration: Stay on the bank and test the act. Barges do not blink, breathe, or twitch their ropes. Pick a test. The ABANDONED sign looks nervous.

interaction_gate_hum_response_hum.narration: A low hum joins the shared beat. You have practiced keeping together. At the frogfolk weir, it will give you a longer moment to move.

interaction_gate_hum_response_tap.narration: Tap, tap. A steady beat holds the sounds together. You have practiced keeping together. At the frogfolk weir, it will give you a longer moment to move.

interaction_gate_hum_response_breathe.narration: A slow breath leaves room for the next sound. You have practiced keeping together. At the frogfolk weir, it will give you a longer moment to move.

interaction_wisp_crowd_response_hum.narration: The wisps sway together, glowing slow and gold. They settle into a soft line behind the raft. "Three coins for the calm," says the cousin in three hats.

interaction_wisp_crowd_response_juggle.narration: The wisps follow the cattails with their whole bodies. They settle into a soft line behind the raft. "Three coins for the calm," says the cousin in three hats.

interaction_wisp_crowd_response_lantern.narration: The wisps circle it, politely, like moths with manners. They settle into a soft line behind the raft. "Three coins for the calm," says the cousin in three hats.

interaction_barge_audience_response_blin.narration: The barnacle blinks first. It has eyelashes. "Mire mimic!" you say. The barge unfolds and slinks into the reeds. You never had to step aboard.

interaction_barge_audience_response_brea.narration: The whole deck rises, then holds its breath. "Mire mimic!" you say. The barge unfolds and slinks into the reeds. You never had to step aboard.

interaction_barge_audience_response_rope.narration: The rope twitches. It is a tail, having a difficult day. "Mire mimic!" you say. The barge unfolds and slinks away. You never had to step aboard.

interaction_gate_hum_response_help.narration: Gullet hums under your sounds. You practice the shared beat with her help, ready for the weir.

interaction_barge_audience_response_help.narration: Gullet helps you compare what you saw. Together you name the mire mimic. It leaves the stage with a wounded sigh.

voiceGuide.tone: warm, foggy, a little spooky but never scary; the marsh knows something and won't say it
forbidden: explaining what the Hollow Gate is

npcVoices.gullet: frogfolk ferrywoman; unhurried, hums between sentences, never says the worrying thing out loud, very proud of her notched hat
npcVoices.nan_rummage: a boggart; talks sideways to the lost things she is sorting, never answers the question you asked, adores a really good sound
npcVoices.wisp: cannot speak; blinks, bobs, sulks and brightens, and is completely undone by the word please
npcVoices.mire_mimic: never speaks; sighs like an actor who just read a bad review
npcVoices.gullets_cousins: the frogfolk ribbon crew; loud, cheerful, all talk at once, the one in three stacked hats is in charge
npcVoices.prospectors: three soggy prospectors; gloomy, dripping, very polite once rescued, the tallest one mourns his hat
npcVoices.sausage_seller: a rush-road sausage seller stuck in the mud; out of breath, generous, shouts everything

interaction_lantern.narration: Back on the raft, the light is going and the fog is coming in. Gullet has one lantern lit, and it needs to get from the stern to the hook at the bow before the fog swallows the whole raft. "Pass it along," she says. "Slowly. Fog loves a flame that is hurrying."

interaction.cue: Catch the lantern, then pass it down the raft.

onSuccess.narration: The lantern reaches the bow without so much as a flicker. Gullet hangs it on its hook, and the fog stops at the edge of its glow like a shy cat. "Good hands," she says, and presses a jar of mosslight into your pack. "Fog gets thick past here. Take it."

onFailure.narration: The lantern wobbles, flickers and goes out with a small pop. Gullet relights it with a sigh and carries it the last bit herself. "Fog loves a hurrying flame," she says. She does not say I told you so, but her hat does.

onAssisted.narration: Gullet walks the lantern down the raft beside you, steady as a heron, and hangs it on its hook. The fog stops at the edge of its glow. She tucks a jar of mosslight into your pack for later.

interaction_gate_hum.narration: Choose a sound to add to the group's practice. Hum, tap a knee, or breathe a steady beat. The frog supplies a loud final croak, whether invited or not. This is practice for keeping together, not a test of who sings best.

interaction.cue: Each connected hero adds a sound to the shared practice.

options.label: Hum a low note
options.reaction: A low hum joins the shared beat.

options.label: Tap the beat on a knee
options.reaction: Tap, tap. A steady beat holds the sounds together.

options.label: Breathe with the beat
options.reaction: A slow breath leaves room for the next sound.

onSuccess.narration: You have practiced keeping a beat together. If you choose the frogfolk weir, this gives you a wider moment to move. The Gate keeps its own counsel.

onFailure.narration: The frog supplies the beat, and you practice together.

onAssisted.narration: Gullet hums underneath your sounds. You practice the shared beat with help, ready for the weir.

interaction_wisp_crowd.narration: Past the ribbon, a crowd of the new wisps has followed your raft, bumping it like puppies. "Keep them busy till the island!" calls the cousin in three hats. "Bored wisps tie knots in things. Last week they tied my hats together." She tosses a handful of coins onto the raft as a down payment.

interaction.cue: Do something friendly until the wisps settle down.

options.label: Hum a lullaby
options.reaction: The wisps sway together, glowing slow and gold.

options.label: Juggle three cattails
options.reaction: The wisps follow the cattails with their whole bodies.

options.label: Hold up a lantern for them to circle
options.reaction: The wisps circle it, politely, like moths with manners.

stages: A few wisps stop bumping the raft.
Most of the crowd is drifting along calmly.
Every wisp is glowing soft and sleepy.

onSuccess.narration: The wisps settle into a long, soft line behind the raft, glowing like a string of lanterns. The cousin in three hats gives you a nod and a tip. "Three coins for the calm," she says. "Don't tell the others."

onFailure.narration: The wisps settle into a long, soft line behind the raft, glowing like a string of lanterns. The cousin in three hats gives you a nod and a tip. "Three coins for the calm," she says. "Don't tell the others."

interaction_barge_audience.narration: Stay on the bank and help test the act. Barges do not blink, breathe, or twitch their ropes. Tell the table what you are watching, then try a test. The sign ABANDONED is looking increasingly nervous.

interaction.cue: Each hero tests one suspicious part from the bank.

options.label: Challenge a barnacle to a staring contest
options.reaction: The barnacle blinks first. It has eyelashes.

options.label: Count the deck's slow breaths
options.reaction: The whole deck rises, then holds its breath.

options.label: Ask the rope to wag
options.reaction: The rope twitches. It is a tail, having a difficult day.

onSuccess.narration: "Mire mimic," you agree. Exposed by its audience, the barge unfolds and slinks into the reeds. You never had to step onto it.

onFailure.narration: Gullet points out a blinking barnacle. Together you name the mire mimic, which leaves in embarrassment.

onAssisted.narration: Gullet helps compare what you saw. Together you name the mire mimic. It leaves the stage with a wounded sigh.
